definitions.explanation: The last of the three terms in the Japanese school year, running roughly from early January to late March. It is the shortest term and ends with graduation and the close of the school year.

examples.japanese: {三学期|さんがっき}が{始|はじ}まった。
{三学期|さんがっき}は{短|みじか}いので、あっという{間|ま}に{終|お}わる。
examples.english: The third term is short, so it's over in no time.

examples.japanese: {三学期|さんがっき}の{成績|せいせき}は、{卒業|そつぎょう}{後|ご}の{進路|しんろ}にも{関係|かんけい}してくる。
examples.english: Your third-term grades also affect your path after graduation.

notes:
{三|さん} (three) + {学期|がっき} (school term). Note the sound change: {学期|がっき} keeps its reading, but the compound is read さんがっき, not さんがくき.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三学期|さんがっき}が{始|はじ}まる: the third term begins
- {三学期|さんがっき}の{終業式|しゅうぎょうしき}: the closing ceremony of the third term
- {三学期|さんがっき}{制|せい}: the three-term system

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
Most Japanese elementary and junior high schools divide the year into {一学期|いちがっき} (April–July), {二学期|にがっき} (September–December), and {三学期|さんがっき} (January–March). Some schools have moved to a two-semester {二期制|にきせい} system, in which case {三学期|さんがっき} does not exist.
